newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to cut corporate tax for banks.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to cut corporate tax for banks.

text.p: Bangladesh Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria on Thursday proposed cutting corporate tax for banks, insurance, financial institutions and non-resident companies to 40 percent for fiscal 1997/98 starting on July 1 from 45 percent.
At present, publicly traded companies are taxed at 35 percent and the non-publicly traded companies at 40 percent.

"To rationalise and to make the corporate tax structure more equitable, I propose a uniform tax rate of 40 percent for non-publicly traded companies, banks, insurance companies, financial institutions and non-resident companies," he told parliament while presenting budget for 1997/98.
He said it might attract foreign investment in Bangladesh.
